text.p: Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger's market-moving comment that he was "relieved" by the Swiss franc's decline pertained to the franc's past moves and was not a forecast for the future, a ministry spokesman said.
The spokesman, in response to an enquiry, also emphasised that the Swiss National Bank (SNB) is charged with foreign exchange policy in Switzerland.

"He (Villiger) said that interest rates have been traditionally low in Switzerland, and he was relieved that the Swiss franc has weakened," spokesman Hugo Schittenhelm said, summarising Villiger's remarks on Monday to a wire service.
The spokesman added that Villiger regarded the franc's decline as a "normalisation" from past levels.
"He said only that it was a justified normalisation. He said nothing about the future," Schittenhelm added.
"If he had said that he expected a further decline, that would have been explosive," Schittenhelm said.
"For that reason, it surprises me if markets took his comments in the context of the future," he added.
He also emphasised that in Switzerland the finance ministry is not directly charged with currency policy, which falls under the aegis of the central bank.
"In Switzerland, the central bank is autonomous," Schittenhelm said.

"It is responsible for currency and monetary policy. Together with the Swiss cabinet, it sets policy. We place a great deal of value on the fact that the central bank remains autonomous, and independent from politics," Schittenhelm said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
